title: Evidence accumulation relates to perceptual consciousness and monitoring
description: EEG recordings from 20 healthy participants performing a tactile detection task with confidence ratings, plus ECoG from one patient with intractable epilepsy. The data were collected to study how evidence accumulation relates to perceptual consciousness and metacognitive monitoring. Near-threshold vibrotactile stimuli were delivered to the right wrist, with detection and confidence reports collected over 500 trials per participant.
methods_description: Near-threshold 230 Hz, 100 ms vibrotactile stimuli were applied to the right wrist, with intensity set by an adaptive staircase seeded from an individual threshold estimate. Participants reported detection and then confidence on a visual analog scale. EEG was recorded from 62 active electrodes (ANT Neuro WaveGuard) at 1024 Hz with EOG and an audio channel for stimulus realignment. The patient's ECoG was recorded from a 24-electrode grid at 2048 Hz.
